name: EM2-16-a-degenerate-triangle-has-a-facing
note: This one survived the first campaign and taught the pin what the guard is really for. A zero-area triangle is dropped by MIN_TRI_AREA anyway - but a NaN vertex gives area NaN, and `NaN < MIN_TRI_AREA` is FALSE, so it lands in the list at y NaN and drags a storey to nowhere. Only `!(len > 0)` catches it.
why: DISC22-G wrote the facing test as `!(up >= FLOOR_NY)`, which rejects a NaN facing on its own - a NaN vertex's triangle is dropped there whether this guard stands or not, and a zero-area one is dropped by MIN_TRI_AREA. The guard stays as the statement of the rule; its pin (the NaN vertex) still holds through the facing test.

name: EM2-18-a-triangle-lands-on-the-lowest-storey-rather-than-the-nearest

why: <= and < pick the same storey unless two storeys are exactly equidistant, which deriveFloors' own minGap makes unreachable: two storeys that close together are one run.
